The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and running Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
I’ll give you both:

1. **`gcloud` CLI** – the easiest way if you already have the Cloud SDK installed.  
2. **REST API** – the raw HTTP request you could send from any HTTP client (curl, Postman, your own script, etc.).

> ⚠️ **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * You need a service account key or OAuth token with `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` (or higher) and `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`.  
> * The **GPU quota** for the RTX A6000 must be available in the zone you choose (e.g., `us-central1-a`).  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣ Authenticate (if you haven’t already)
gcloud auth login
gcloud config set project YOUR_PROJECT_ID
gcloud config set compute/zone us-central1-a   # pick your preferred zone

# 2️⃣ Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
    --machine-type n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
    --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size 100GB \
    --boot-disk-type pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy TERMINATE \
    --restart-on-failure \
    --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
        sudo reboot' \
    --tags http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs & 30 GB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. `type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1` requests one RTX A6000. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Selects the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu Cloud image project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy TERMINATE` | If the host machine is reclaimed, the VM is terminated (default is MIGRATE). |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts the VM if it crashes. |
| `--metadata startup-script` | Installs the NVIDIA driver on first boot and reboots. |
| `--tags` | Opens ports 80/443 for HTTP/HTTPS traffic (adjust as needed). |

> **Tip:** If you prefer a different machine type (e.g., `n1-highmem-16`), just change the `--machine-type` value.

---

## 2. Using the REST API

Below is a **JSON payload** you can POST to the Compute Engine API.  
Replace `YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, and `YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL` with your actual values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "TERMINATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nsudo reboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {
          "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT",
          "name": "External NAT"
        }
      ],
      "tags": ["http-server", "https-server"]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "YOUR_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Making the request with `curl`

```bash
# 1️⃣ Get an OAuth 2.0 access token (replace with your method)
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣ POST the JSON payload
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **Note:**  
> * The `acceleratorType` URL uses the **project** and **zone** of the instance.  
> * The `sourceImage` URL points to the Ubuntu 20.04 LTS family.  
> * The `serviceAccounts` section grants the instance full Cloud Platform access; adjust scopes if you want tighter security.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Project ID & zone set |
| ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled |
| ✅ | GPU quota for RTX A6000 available |
| ✅ | Service account with proper scopes |
| ✅ | `gcloud` CLI or OAuth token ready |
| ✅ | JSON payload or CLI command prepared |

Once you run either the `gcloud` command or the REST API request, the instance will spin up, install the NVIDIA driver, and reboot automatically. After the reboot, you can SSH into the VM and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu@EXTERNAL_IP
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. 🎉

Let me know if you’d like help automating this with Terraform, Deployment Manager, or another IaC tool!
